decisions.reason: The pegboard-back display has not been shown on the website since 2018, which suggests weak results against aspirations; with paper and energy costs squeezing margins in 2022, the slack that justified carrying it is gone.
The standard quarter-pallet shelf display is a staple of the firm's one-stop display offer and likely remains part of customer orders even without its own web page, so it probably meets aspirations.
The eighth-pallet format shares tooling and processes with the quarter-pallet line at low extra cost, so it is likely kept as a complementary size despite less visibility on the website.

The wooden pallet lies outside the cardboard core, has not been visible since 2018, and faces rising timber costs, so problemistic search under cost pressure points to moving its resources back to the core business.
Demand for media-product displays is declining structurally and the product has had no visible presence since 2018, so a performance shortfall is likely and its resources are better used elsewhere.
